title: Home
subtitle: Your projects on this computer — save versions, upload to GitHub and stay up to date, without a single command.

empty.title: Your projects, without the command line
empty.body: Pick a folder on this computer. Home keeps track of every change, saves versions and uploads them to GitHub — on a button press or automatically.
empty.step3: Save & upload — by button or automatically

state.notUploaded_one: {{count}} saved version not on GitHub yet
state.notUploaded_other: {{count}} saved versions not on GitHub yet
state.branchNew: This branch isn't on GitHub yet — upload it
state.allGood: Everything saved and up to date
state.repoGone: The GitHub repo is gone — choose what to do

actions.openEditor: Open in code editor (VS Code, VSCodium, Zed, Sublime)

strip.notPushed: This branch isn't on GitHub yet

changes.emptyHint: Edit files in your folder — changes show up here within seconds.
changes.secretsWarn: Some of these look like secrets (keys, .env). Untick them or mark them as not shared before uploading.

files.hint: Ticked = goes to GitHub. Unticked = stays only on this computer.
files.suggestBody: Found in your folder. Most projects keep these off GitHub.
files.untracked: “{{path}}” will be removed from GitHub with your next save — it stays on your computer.
files.blocked: The folder “{{parent}}” isn't shared — share it first.

reference.what: The reference is the original project you copied or forked. See what's new there, and what only your copy has (your own fixes).
reference.onlyYours: Only in your copy — your own changes
reference.getLatest: Bring the reference's changes into my copy
reference.unrelated: This folder was copied instead of cloned, so its history isn't connected to the reference. You can still see what's new there.
reference.notSet: No reference set — add one in Settings.
reference.upToDate: You have everything the reference has.

branch.label: Branch
branch.hint: A branch is a separate line of work — try things without touching main.
branch.carried_one: Your unsaved change came along — it's still there to save here.
branch.carried_other: Your {{count}} unsaved changes came along — they're still there to save here.

latest.merged: Combined the latest changes with yours

settings.name: Name
settings.referenceHint: e.g. the original you copied — only for comparing, never uploaded to

autoModeHint.interval_one: Saves a version every minute while there are changes.
autoModeHint.interval_other: Saves a version every {{count}} minutes while there are changes.
autoModeHint.idle_one: Saves once you haven't changed anything for a minute.
autoModeHint.idle_other: Saves once you haven't changed anything for {{count}} minutes.

settings.removeHint: The folder and its files stay exactly as they are.
settings.needsWatch: Turn on watching to save automatically.
settings.invalidRepo: Use owner/name or a GitHub link

addDialog.title: Add a project folder
addDialog.plainBody: Home will set up Git for this folder and save a first version.
addDialog.name: Name
addDialog.private: Private — only you can see it
addDialog.referenceHint: The original project, if this is a copy — to see what's new there
addDialog.already: This folder is already in Home

ghTabs.noRepoBody: Choose the GitHub repo this folder uploads to in Settings — then you can edit its About box, publish releases and run Actions from here.

about.descriptionPlaceholder: What is this project? One or two sentences.
about.websiteHint: https:// is added if you leave it out
about.topicsPlaceholder:
rust, desktop-app, gui
— or one per line
about.topicsHint: Separate with commas or put each on its own line. Spaces become hyphens, capitals become lowercase.

releases.keptDraft: Some files failed — the release stays a draft until you publish it
releases.tagExists: Existing tag (commit {{sha}}) — the release uses it
releases.title: Title
releases.notesPlaceholder: What changed? Markdown works. Or let GitHub write it from the merged pull requests.
releases.draft: Save as draft (only you can see it)
releases.draftHint: Files you add are uploaded before the release goes public.
releases.filesHint: Installers, zips, binaries… shown under the release for download.
releases.emptyBody: A release is a named version people can download — with notes on what changed and files like installers attached.
releases.tagKept: The tag is kept — delete it below if you don't need it.
releases.confirmDeleteWithTag: Click again — deletes release and tag
releases.tagOn: On the latest uploaded version of {{branch}}
releases.tagsHint: A tag marks a version. New tags point at the latest uploaded version of {{branch}}.
releases.notUploadedWarn_one: {{count}} saved version isn't on GitHub yet — the release won't include it.
releases.notUploadedWarn_other: {{count}} saved versions aren't on GitHub yet — the release won't include them.

actionsTab.startedBody: It shows up below in a few seconds.
actionsTab.notManual: This workflow can't be started by hand — it has no workflow_dispatch trigger.
actionsTab.notUploaded: in your folder — not uploaded yet
actionsTab.addedBody: Save & upload in Changes to switch it on.
actionsTab.addNote: Written into your folder — it starts working after your next upload.
actionsTab.clash: A workflow with this file name already exists.

blank.name: Blank workflow
blank.what: A minimal starting point you fill in yourself.

ci-node.name: Test a Node.js project
ci-node.what: Installs, builds and runs npm test on every push.

ci-rust.name: Test a Rust project
ci-rust.what: cargo build + cargo test on every push, with caching.

release-files.name: Attach a source zip to releases
release-files.what: Every release you publish gets a .zip of the code.

pages.name: Publish a website (GitHub Pages)
pages.what: Puts the folder online as a website on every push.

manual.name: A task you start by hand
manual.what: Example with a dropdown, a switch and a text field.

gone.pushTitle: The GitHub repo {{repo}} doesn't exist anymore
gone.pushBody: It was deleted, or your account lost access. Your files here are safe — choose where uploads should go now.
gone.recreateHint: Creates a new private repo with the same name and uploads everything from this folder.
gone.disconnected: This project now stays on this computer only
gone.renamed: The repo was renamed or moved: {{from}} → {{to}}
gone.refGone: The reference repo {{repo}} doesn't exist anymore

wf.confirmDelete: Click again to delete the file
wf.deletedBody: Save & upload in Changes to remove it on GitHub too.
wf.fromGitHub: This workflow isn't in your folder yet — you're editing GitHub's copy; saving puts it into your folder.
wf.badName: File name: letters, digits, - _ . and ending in .yml
wf.saveAnyway: There's a problem in the file — you can still save it

problem.yaml: This isn't valid YAML (check indentation — spaces, not tabs)
problem.notMap: A workflow must start with keys like name:, on: and jobs:
problem.noOn: Missing "on:" — when should it run? (e.g. on: push)

clone.whereHint: each repository gets its own subfolder
clone.note: Each clone becomes a Home project that uploads back to its repository. A folder that already exists and isn't empty is skipped, never overwritten.

diff.none: No line changes (only the mode or a rename)
diff.truncated: Only the first 5,000 lines are shown

park.hint: Puts every unsaved change aside and takes the folder back to the last save — bring them back any time
park.doneBody: The folder is back at your last save. Find them under "Parked" to bring them back.

undo.hint: Takes back the newest save while it's only on this computer. Its changes come back as unsaved edits — nothing on disk changes.
undo.doneBody: Its changes are unsaved edits again, with the same message ready.
undo.doneBodyPlain: Its changes are unsaved edits again — find them under Changes.
undo.fromHint_one: Takes back this version — its changes become unsaved again, nothing on disk changes
undo.fromHint_other: Takes back {{count}} versions — this one and all newer ones. Their changes become unsaved again; nothing on disk changes.
undo.manyDoneBody: Their changes are unsaved again — save them as one clean version from Changes.

conflicts.title: Both sides changed the same files
conflicts.intro: These files were changed here and on GitHub in ways that can't be combined automatically. Pick whose version to keep for each one — everything else is combined as usual.
conflicts.footer: You can still change any file afterwards and save again.
